cards.text: Judah is in a drought, and the LORD has told Jeremiah, a prophet, not to pray for the well-being of this people (Jeremiah 14:1, 11). Now the LORD gives Jeremiah a word to speak to them. It starts with eyes that overflow with tears, day and night, and friend, this one is heavy.
The tears are "for the virgin daughter of my people" who "has been shattered by a crushing blow, a severely grievous wound."

cards.question: In this word, going out to the country means seeing those slain by the sword. What does entering the city show?
In the word Jeremiah speaks, both prophet and priest travel to a land they do not know.

cards.text: Then a prayer goes up, and it opens with hard questions: "Have You rejected Judah completely? Do You despise Zion?…"

cards.question: The prayer says they hoped for ___, but no good has come.

cards.text: No peace. And the time of healing they hoped for? Only terror.

cards.question: As the prayer goes on, the ones praying say the guilt belongs only to their fathers, not to themselves.
The ones praying ask the LORD, for the sake of His name, not to despise them or disgrace His glorious throne. Then they ask Him to remember something and not break it. What is it?

cards.text: Then the prayer turns to rain. And friend, in a drought, that's the question EVERYBODY is asking.

cards.question: In the middle of the drought, the prayer asks who brings the rain. What answer does it give?

cards.text: So they put their hope in the LORD, "for You have done all these things." The prayer even calls the idols worthless, and friend, I get it: I spent YEARS stuck in a junk drawer, and not ONE dead battery in there ever lit up the dark.
Then the LORD speaks to Jeremiah. I think this one hurts, friend.

cards.question: The LORD says even if two men from Israel's past stood before Him, His heart would not go out to this people. Who are they?

cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, and Samuel, a prophet. Even if they stood before Him, the LORD says, "Send them from My presence, and let them go!"

cards.question: If the people ask Jeremiah, "Where shall we go?" the LORD gives him a safe place to point them to.

cards.text: Instead, each one goes where they're destined: to death, to the sword, to famine or to captivity.
Then the LORD names four kinds of destroyers He will appoint over them: the sword, the dogs, the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth.

cards.question: The LORD says He will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, because of what one king did in Jerusalem. Which king?

cards.text: Then the LORD asks, "Who will have pity on you, O Jerusalem? Who will mourn for you? Who will turn aside to ask about your welfare?"

cards.question: The LORD tells Jerusalem that she has forsaken Him and turned her back.
So the LORD will stretch out His hand against Jerusalem and destroy her. He says He is weary of showing ___.

cards.text: Then a picture from harvest time: He will scatter them with a winnowing fork at the gates of the land.

cards.question: The LORD says He will bereave and destroy His people. Which ones?

answers.text: Those who have not turned from their ways
Those who live in the far villages
Those who fled from Jerusalem first

cards.question: The LORD says Judah's widows will be so few that you could count them on one hand.

cards.text: More numerous than the sand of the sea. And He will bring a destroyer at noon against the mothers of young men, with anguish and dismay all of a sudden.

cards.question: The LORD says the mother of seven will grow faint and breathe her last breath. What else does He say she will face?

cards.text: Her sun, the LORD says, will set while it is still day. And the rest He will put to the sword in the presence of their enemies.
